qa.text: The reset, for testing: open this and the start screen says every board is fresh again, and today’s board plays as a first visit, how-to and all (Settings stay). Use it whenever you want to play today’s board again.

Your field: tap Practice, pick RT and deal. About 6 of the 19 tiles come from RT (pay, schools, NBRC pass rates, the RT compact, vent and oxygen math); pharmacy gets about 4. Do they feel like your field, and is any question in the wrong field? Make a board has the same row, and its link carries it.

50:50: open a tile with four answers and tap 50:50 under them. Two wrong answers go and the key says Used; it works once a board, so on the next tile it is off. The i at the end of the row explains all three lifelines. Are the same two answers left on your phone and a desk? On a phone the lifelines took the row Back to the board had: the X and your back gesture close the card.

Hint: on a tile that has one, tap Hint and one line shows under the question. A state question gets the 50-state median, a compact question how many states have joined, the bedside math its formula or first step. Does it help without giving the answer away? On a tile with no hint the key is off and the i says why.

Swap: tap it on a question you would rather skip. A new one comes from the same zone and just as hard, so your route holds, and the tile's label follows it. Then finish and press Share: the last line says 1 lifeline, 2 or 3; a board that used none says nothing, so a clean board stands out.
Open the game. One brass button plays today's board; under it, Make a board, Practice and Past boards. Is it clear what to do first?

Play today's board on your phone. Start on any top tile and work down to the bottom row. Does the board fit the screen with nothing to scroll, and can you tell which tiles you hold and which are closed?

The question card: four keys or two keys, and a number is four answers to pick from, sized so you can tell the right one by scale, with the bedside math as near misses. Can you answer most without looking anything up? After you answer, is the answer card enough: right and wrong marked, the exact figure, one line of why, the source and date, and the link into the site?

No dots: crossing is the win, and the result is your time and your misses, as in Crossed in 1:42 and 1 miss. Every tile is worth the same and the compass is just the middle tile, so the route is about which questions you can answer. A board with no clock (a past day, a made board) counts up instead. Does a fast, clean crossing feel like a good board?

No time limit and no miss limit: a miss closes that tile and you route around it, the clock counts up from your first tile, and the board ends when you cross or no way is left. Your result is your time and your misses. Does crossing still feel like a race?
Finish a board, press Share and paste the line into a text to yourself. Does it read right and give nothing away?
Make a board: pick a clock and the misses, copy the link, and open it on another device. Same board?
The normals are drafts for your check as an RRT. The question list shows every one with its source; mark any range you would change.
The questions: skim the whole list. Is the mix right across the seven zones? Anything that should not be in a trivia game?
On a desk: the board on the left and the question on the right. Does it read at a glance?
Switch the site to the day theme and play a practice board. Do the tiles still read?
